item.question: Is it possible to reason out if the sides are equal or not, and if the angles are right or not, without using any measuring instruments in the above figure? Can we do this by only looking at the position of corners in the dot grid?
steps_tex: Count how many dots across and how many down it takes to go from one corner to the next.

concept_name: Constructing a square of side 6 cm

item.question: How would you construct a square with a side of 6 cm? A square PQRS of side length 6 cm is constructed.
steps: Draw PQ = 6 cm with a ruler.
Place the protractor with its centre at P and its baseline along PQ, mark 90° and draw a perpendicular through P.
Mark S on this perpendicular so that PS = 6 cm (ruler), or open the compass to 6 cm, tip at P, and mark an arc.
At Q draw the perpendicular to PQ and mark R with QR = 6 cm (with the compass: keep the radius at 6 cm and put the tip at Q).
Join R and S. Check RS = 6 cm, ∠R = 90°, ∠S = 90°.
item.answer: Square PQRS with PQ = QR = RS = SP = 6 cm and all angles 90°. RS = 6 cm and ∠R = ∠S = 90°.
item.text:

Answer: Square PQRS with PQ = QR = RS = SP = 6 cm and all angles 90°. RS = 6 cm and ∠R = ∠S = 90°.

item.question: Construct a rectangle that can be divided into 3 identical squares (a rectangle split by two vertical lines into three equal squares).
steps_tex: Choose the square side, say $3\text{ cm}$.
Draw a rough diagram showing $3$ equal squares side by side.
Draw $AB = 3\text{ cm}$, draw perpendiculars at $A$ and $B$, and mark $AD = 3\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 3\text{ cm}$.
Use the compass to transfer the $3\text{ cm}$ length along the line two more times so that the total length is $9\text{ cm}$.
Draw the dividing lines to check each part is a $3\text{ cm}$ square.
item.answer_tex: Any rectangle whose length is $3$ times its breadth, for example $9\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$. Each square has side $3\text{ cm}$.

extra_items.question: Construct a rectangle ACDF that can be divided into two identical squares ABEF and BCDE, with no measurements imposed. If AF is assigned 4 cm, what must the length of AC be?
steps_tex: Draw a rough diagram: $AB = BC$ and $FE = ED$, and all the short lines are equal $(AF = AB = BE = FE = BC = CD = ED)$.
Draw $AF = 4\text{ cm}$.
Draw a line perpendicular to $AF$ at $A$. With the compass tip at $A$ and radius $AF$, mark $B$ on this line.
Keep the same radius and mark $C$ beyond $B$ so that $BC = AF$.
Do the same at $F$ to place the other corners and complete the rectangle $ACDF$.
extra_items.answer_tex: $AC = 8\text{ cm}$. The rectangle is $8\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$.
steps: Draw a rough diagram: AB = BC and FE = ED, and all the short lines are equal (AF = AB = BE = FE = BC = CD = ED).
Draw AF = 4 cm.
Draw a line perpendicular to AF at A. With the compass tip at A and radius AF, mark B on this line.
Keep the same radius and mark C beyond B so that BC = AF.
Do the same at F to place the other corners and complete the rectangle ACDF.
extra_items.answer: AC = 8 cm. The rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm.
extra_items.text:
$1$. Draw a rough diagram: $AB = BC$ and $FE = ED$, and all the short lines are equal $(AF = AB = BE = FE = BC = CD = ED)$.
$2$. Draw $AF = 4\text{ cm}$.
$3$. Draw a line perpendicular to $AF$ at $A$. With the compass tip at $A$ and radius $AF$, mark $B$ on this line.
$4$. Keep the same radius and mark $C$ beyond $B$ so that $BC = AF$.
$5$. Do the same at $F$ to place the other corners and complete the rectangle $ACDF$.
Answer: $AC = 8\text{ cm}$. The rectangle is $8\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$.

item.question: Give the lengths of the sides of a rectangle that cannot be divided into two identical squares, and of a rectangle that cannot be divided into three identical squares. a) Cannot be divided into two identical squares b) Cannot be divided into three identical squares
steps_tex: A rectangle splits into two identical squares only if length $= 2 \times$ breadth.
$4\text{ cm}$ is not $2 \times 2.5\text{ cm}$.
It splits into three only if length $= 3 \times$ breadth; $7\text{ cm}$ is not $3 \times 2\text{ cm}$.
item.answer_tex: $(a)$: for example $4\text{ cm}$ by $2.5\text{ cm}$, $(b)$: for example $7\text{ cm}$ by $2\text{ cm}$ (other answers possible)
steps: A rectangle splits into two identical squares only if length = 2 × breadth.
4 cm is not 2 × 2.5 cm.
It splits into three only if length = 3 × breadth; 7 cm is not 3 × 2 cm.
item.answer: a) for example 4 cm by 2.5 cm, b) for example 7 cm by 2 cm (other answers possible)
item.text:
$1$. A rectangle splits into two identical squares only if length $= 2 \times$ breadth.
$2$. $4\text{ cm}$ is not $2 \times 2.5\text{ cm}$.
$3$. It splits into three only if length $= 3 \times$ breadth; $7\text{ cm}$ is not $3 \times 2\text{ cm}$.
Answer: $(a)$: for example $4\text{ cm}$ by $2.5\text{ cm}$, $(b)$: for example $7\text{ cm}$ by $2\text{ cm}$ (other answers possible)

item.question: Construct a rectangle of sides 8 cm and 4 cm. How will you construct a square inside, as shown in the figure, such that the centre of the square is the same as the centre of the rectangle? (The square touches the top and bottom of the rectangle and sits in the middle of its length.)
steps_tex: Draw the $8\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ rectangle.
The square must fit between top and bottom, so its side is $4\text{ cm}$.
Leave $(8\text{ cm} - 4\text{ cm}) \div 2 = 2\text{ cm}$ on each side.
Mark points $2\text{ cm}$ in from each short side and draw the vertical lines of the square.
item.answer_tex: The square has side $4\text{ cm}$. Its left and right sides are $2\text{ cm}$ away from the left and right sides of the rectangle.
steps: Draw the 8 cm by 4 cm rectangle.
The square must fit between top and bottom, so its side is 4 cm.
Leave (8 cm − 4 cm) ÷ 2 = 2 cm on each side.
Mark points 2 cm in from each short side and draw the vertical lines of the square.
item.answer: The square has side 4 cm. Its left and right sides are 2 cm away from the left and right sides of the rectangle.
